audience: Engineers seeking the relationship between DFlash parallel draft distributions and DDTree target verification.
prerequisites: Products and sums of small probabilities.
objective: Relate parallel marginal proposals to a budgeted prefix tree and distinguish draft coverage from target-selected committed output.
scope: The combined example's algorithmic argument, with partial narration mapping; no automatic approval of legacy numerical graphics or end-to-end rendering.
assumptions: Q1, Q2 and Q3 are toy distributions under fixed shared conditioning.
The root b is an already-emitted anchor and is outside the seven-node proposal budget.
The expected-depth prefix sum is under Q, not a guarantee under the target distribution.
Insertion order is not BFS. Position depth, ancestor visibility and target membership have distinct roles.
Runtime improvement depends on draft, tree-build and verification costs per committed token; accepting two proposals is not measured speedup.
unknowns: Most narration is scene-local and includes loop-generated blocks; only the independently located opening block at rendered index one is mapped here. No event IDs are available.
Older scene products and target-output graphics require review against canonical DDTreeFull; this contract encodes independent expected semantics, not known legacy defects.
No audiovisual review or learner-response evidence is supplied.

claims.statement: A finite budget buys alternative prefixes scored under factorized Q rather than only one modal path.

evidence.support: The surrogate maximizes expected matched depth under Q using prefix masses; root does not count toward B.

claims.statement: A target miss terminates cached reuse but is appended as valid output and the next anchor.

evidence.locator: follow_verified_tree; ddtree_generate accepted_tokens and next_token output assignments
evidence.support: The first nonmember next_token is returned separately and written after matched tokens; only matched indices retain current target KV entries.

claims.statement: The worked seventh prefix a-model-works has exact mass 0.1092; rounded 0.109 is approximate.

evidence.support: The input values 0.35, 0.60 and 0.52 yield the independently checked exact product.

worked_examples.description: Preserve exact arithmetic despite rounded visual labels.
Reconstruct tree membership from token-array paths and supplied target choices; root b is excluded from new output.

mapping_note: Only opening()'s second narration block has an explicit rendered index/text mapping. Later stable contract beat IDs are conceptual source-stage mappings, not invented runtime event IDs.

beats.purpose: Connect cheap block drafting to multiple likely continuations.

narration.text: DFlash makes drafting cheap by predicting a whole block in parallel. DDTree then spends the verifier budget on several likely continuations, instead of betting everything on one path.

beats.purpose: The tree-construction stage must distinguish exact products from rounded labels.
tree_verification follows a and model, then emits the missing runs as the new anchor.

transfer_questions.question: If increasing B improves the sum of draft prefix masses, has it proved lower wall-clock time per output token?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. The sum is a Q-based coverage surrogate. Drafting, tree construction, verification cost and actual target-selected output must also be considered.
transfer_questions.justification: A larger nonnegative prefix sum cannot establish a runtime inequality. The denominator is actual committed tokens, whereas the numerator includes work that generally increases with tree size. The paper distinguishes the surrogate from the target objective.

transfer_questions.question: Why is runs emitted even though it is not a child of a-model?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: Because the target selected it at that prefix. Only cached continuation stops; the token remains valid output and anchors the next round.
transfer_questions.justification: Direct membership testing reaches [a,model], finds no [a,model,runs], and returns runs separately. The official output assignment appends that returned token.
